title: An unattributed story about a proposed action lets its source test public tolerance before committing and still deny it was a test
body:
- A politician floats a controversial proposal through indirect media coverage — a leak, rumor, or unattributed story — rather than announcing it on the record.
- Public reaction to the story functions as a measurement of tolerance for the underlying action.
- The actor uses that measurement to decide whether to commit to a similar action in future votes.
- The unattributed form leaves the actor's role off the record, so the testing carries no public commitment.
- Case: Politicians float policy proposals through media stories to gauge public tolerance before committing to the legislation.
conversion: An unattributed story about a possible action becomes a tolerance test, and the unattributed status turns the test into something the source can disavow.
